technical_hypothesis.interaction_pattern: batch or online human-in-the-loop ranking after deterministic eligibility filtering
technical_hypothesis.primary_training_data_risk: historical exposure and engagement are strongly biased by previous placement, marketing, catalog availability and editorial choices, while sparse long-tail titles lack reliable counterfactual outcomes

training_data.observation_unit: an eligible title, program or clip considered for a specific placement, schedule slot or distribution channel
training_data.input_data: confirmed candidates include rights and territory eligibility, availability windows, format, genre, language, editorial metadata, prior exposure and audience events; customer-specific coverage is unknown
training_data.target_or_reward: candidate outcomes could include completed views, qualified watch time, retention, circulation across services or editor-approved placement; the correct objective and trade-offs are unknown
training_data.label_source: platform exposure and consumption logs plus explicit editorial decisions and corrections; label quality and completeness are unknown
training_data.prediction_time: after deterministic rights, compliance, availability and format checks and before editorial placement or publication
training_data.expected_volume: unknown and likely highly uneven between large platforms, regional broadcasters and independent catalogs
training_data.class_balance: unknown; long-tail titles and rarely selected archive assets are expected to have sparse positive outcomes
training_data.historical_coverage: unknown; prior placements, marketing support and catalog availability may be incompletely recorded
training_data.train_validation_split: time-based and title or franchise-grouped splits would be required to avoid future and near-duplicate leakage
training_data.leakage_risks: using final placement, post-campaign metadata, later rights corrections, completed audience outcomes or editor decisions unavailable at ranking time
training_data.representativeness_risks: audience, platform, device, region, genre, release window and marketing differences can make historical rankings non-transferable
training_data.feedback_loop: ranking changes exposure, which changes future labels and can reinforce already visible titles unless exploration and editorial diversity controls are explicit
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: audience-event data must be minimized and governed under LGPD; editorial, licensing and commercial data may be confidential
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: use deterministic eligibility, editorial collections, transparent business rules, search and manual curation; adopt existing recommendation or media-asset-management capabilities where appropriate

portfolio_comparison.reason: The selected workflows expose real ranking decisions, but title and clip discovery, catalog personalization, metadata enrichment, automated highlight surfacing and editorial curation are established platform capabilities. The Brazilian circulation problem is material, yet a ranking engine does not itself solve licensing, catalog acquisition or regulatory visibility constraints, and no distinct integration boundary or measurable outcome remained beyond adopting or configuring current products.

existing_landscape.summary: Use deterministic rights and compliance filters, editorial curation and existing recommendation or media-asset-management capabilities. Treat circulation of Brazilian works as a catalog, licensing, policy and distribution problem first; evaluate local ranking only as an internal product feature when sufficient unbiased exposure data exists.

research.findings: ANCINE data published in December 2025 confirms low availability and circulation of Brazilian works across leading VoD platforms, but the load-bearing constraint includes catalog presence and licensing rather than only recommendation quality. Current media platforms already provide recommendation, metadata enrichment, archive discovery, automated moment detection and distribution workflows. Research on a Brazilian alternative streaming service also shows editorial curation without intensive datafication as a viable operating model.
